text:
A tourist visited a village in India and noticed something strange. Next to a temple stood a huge elephant. It was tied to a post with only a thin rope. The tourist was amazed. The elephant could easily break the rope and walk away, yet it stood quietly.

He asked the owner, “Why doesn’t he escape? He is so strong!”

The owner smiled. “When he was a baby, we tied him to this same post with the same kind of rope. At that time, it was strong enough to hold him. He pulled and pulled, but he couldn’t break free. After many attempts, he accepted that the rope was stronger than he was.”

“And now?”

“Now he is a grown elephant, but he still believes that he can’t escape. He never tries. In his mind, the rope is as strong as it was twenty years ago.”

The tourist was silent. He remembered a business idea he had never tried because a friend had once told him that it would fail. He thought about all the things he had been afraid to attempt because of a failure long ago.

That evening, he sat in his hotel room and wrote a list of everything that he had given up too early. Then, one by one, he decided to try again.

Moral: Many of the limits in our lives exist only in our minds.
